items.title: Martien de Jong
items.description_seo: Martien has been building software professionally since 2006: hospital systems, government platforms, rail apps, SEO automation. He started as a software developer and IT trainer, and years of work for businesses and non-profits, at home and abroad, taught him that technology only matters when it empowers people. Somewhere along the way the question shifted from "what can I build" to "how is value actually created". ProsperGenics is his answer in progress: a community spanning the Netherlands and Kenya where people create value for themselves and each other, with software as the lever. Every project is a co-creation across borders and cultures: he brings technical expertise and an honest perspective, communities bring local knowledge, creativity and drive. People come first: clear communication, transparency, the courage to learn from failure and the ability to simplify the complex. Today he builds Jengo, the AI agent platform that runs most of what the community ships, and he is open to new connections, whether you are an entrepreneur, investor, changemaker or student.

fields.quote: I'm building Jengo, our AI agent platform. It runs most of what we ship.

items.title: Simitia Mpoe
items.description_seo: Simitia came to the community to build, and that is exactly what she does: web products, design work, her own ventures. As part of the ProsperGenics founding team she leads the team in Kenya, and she is the personal assistant to Martien de Jong. She organises fundraisers for the sick and the elderly. Her newest venture is Maa-Link Ride, a ride-hailing app like Uber or Bolt that she is building. Every project adds a skill, and every skill flows back into her own business. She is one of the clearest examples of the ProsperGenics loop: learn by building, build to create value, reinvest the value in yourself.

fields.quote: I design and build web products, and I'm growing my own business with everything I learn.

items.title: Diko Mohammed
items.description_seo: Diko's talent is seeing the opportunity before anyone else does, and then actually building it. She is a project manager, software developer and tech problem-solver in one: a hybrid of project leadership and hands-on development who turns ideas into scalable digital solutions. With a strong eye for detail and a passion for clean, efficient code, she thrives in fast-paced environments, leading teams and shipping features. She is part of the ProsperGenics founding team and co-founded her own AI company, Afrigentic. Inside the community she develops software; outside it she opens doors: integrations, partnerships, contacts that connect ProsperGenics products to the wider tech world.

fields.role: Founding team, Software Developer, Co-Founder of Afrigentic
fields.quote: I turn opportunities into products. Right now that means integrations and new partnerships.

items.title: Sjoerd Schepman
items.description_seo: Sjoerd curates the Perridon art collection: researching where each work comes from, who held it, and what its story is. With the ProsperGenics team he explores how software can serve that work, from provenance research tooling to making a collection's knowledge accessible.

fields.quote: I curate the Perridon collection, researching the provenance and the stories behind every piece.

items.title: Faith Nkumun
items.description_seo: Faith ran a small store in Oloolaimutia, Kenya. She joined the community to learn the business side of her business: bookkeeping, planning, trade. What she learned, she now applies to take her store further, and what she proves, she passes on to others around her.

fields.quote: I had a small store in Oloolaimutia. Here I learned the business skills to take it further.

items.title: Maxwell
items.description_seo: Maxwell is still studying, and that is precisely his strength: everything he learns in class gets tested the same week on real community projects with real customers. School gives him the theory; the community gives him the practice.

fields.quote: I'm still studying, and I apply what I learn on real projects with real customers.

items.title: Finehas Lesiamon
items.description_seo: Lesiamon was the very first participant in ProsperGenics and is part of its founding team. He carries two of its pillars: he builds software, and he builds the people who build software. New developers in the community learn the craft from him, task by task. His own work blends front-end creativity with back-end logic: WordPress sites and Angular web apps, Node.js back ends, Python with Flask, pages styled with SCSS, intuitive UI/UX and responsive design, GitHub workflows and, more recently, Java and XAMPP environments. His conviction: good software starts with understanding people.

fields.quote: I develop software and train new developers. Good software starts with understanding people.

items.title: Frank Kobaai
items.description_seo: Frank is a Nairobi-based web developer on the ProsperGenics founding team who got real responsibility from day one, and took it. Frank builds and ships features for the community's web platforms: from first commit to live deployment, including this website. Web design and user experience are at the heart of the work: from the first idea to wireframes, from wireframes to Webflow builds, and from there to finished websites, merging design precision with technical expertise. Frank also knows AI well and is keen to share that knowledge, demystifying AI for others.

fields.quote: I build and ship features for our web platforms, with real responsibility from day one.

items.title: Sophy Nashipae de Jong
items.description_seo: Sophy bridges two worlds. She manages Nashipae Cultural Oasis, a cultural centre that preserves and shares Maasai culture: a place for learning, celebration and community. And she is learning Dutch with the community's own coach app, usually as the first user of whatever the team builds next.

fields.quote: I'm learning Dutch with our own coach app. Learning works better when it feels personal.

items.title: Mayiani Nanana Mpoe
items.description_seo: Mayiani is learning digital skills step by step and puts each one to work in daily life. No leap, just steady ground gained: the quiet version of value creation the community is built on.

fields.quote: I'm learning digital skills step by step and putting them to work in daily life.

items.title: Lou Marten
items.description_seo: Lou works on the ProsperGenics brand: the strategy, the story, and the words that make what the community builds understandable to the outside world. Builders make the value; Lou makes it visible.

fields.quote: I work on our brand and marketing, finding the right words for what we build.

items.title: Natumi
items.description_seo: Community members invested in Natumi. She used it to grow her herd, runs it as a working business, and the results now pay the school fees. No app, no code: her story is value creation in its most direct form, and proof of what the community exists to do.

fields.quote: People invested in me. I grew my herd and the results now pay the school fees.

items.title: Timothy Rop
items.description_seo: Timothy brings AI to people who think it is not for them. Through hands-on training sessions he shows that AI tools are accessible, practical and immediately useful - no technical background required.

fields.quote: I help people understand AI and put it to work in their daily business.

items.title: Nico van der Berg
items.description_seo: Nico works at the intersection of data and decision-making. He builds analytics pipelines, trains models and translates the results into decisions businesses can actually act on.

fields.quote: Data tells stories most people miss. I help you read them.

items.title: Farid Harrak
items.description_seo: Farid is a game enthusiast learning to build websites with AI. He combines his passion for gaming with emerging AI technologies to create web experiences, developing his skills in modern, AI-powered web development one project at a time.

fields.quote: I'm learning to build websites with AI, bringing my gaming passion into the web.
